summary: Specifies a data model for sharing data between users with JMAP. Future documents can reference it when defining data types, so sharing works consistently across them.

eli5.summary: This gives one common way for people to share their email, calendars or contacts with each other, so every app does sharing the same way.

questions: what does shareWith do in jmap
subtitle: A common JMAP model for principals, share notifications and per-object sharing rights.

tldr.problem: JMAP syncs mail, calendars and contacts, but had no common way to represent the people and resources data can be shared with, or to express sharing consistently across data types.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines Principal and ShareNotification data types and a framework of three properties, isSubscribed, myRights and shareWith, that shareable data types must include.
tldr.outcome: Future JMAP data type specifications can reference it for a consistent sharing model. It updates RFC 8620.

today: RFC 9670 is a Proposed Standard published in November 2024. It updates RFC 8620 and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: A Shared Model for JMAP
sections.content:
The JSON Meta Application Protocol (JMAP, RFC 8620) synchronizes data such as mail, calendars or contacts between a client and a server. This document defines a data model for entities in a collaborative environment and a framework for sharing data between them.

It does not define what may be shared or how fine-grained permissions are, because that depends on the data type. Those details are left to the documents that define each type.
sections.eli5: It is a shared rulebook for handing out access, while each game decides what the rules mean.

sections.title: Principals
sections.content:
A Principal represents an individual, a group, a location, a resource such as a projector, or another entity. Sharing is generally set up by giving rights on data in an Account to other Principals. Managing the set of Principals is out of scope, since it is domain specific and likely maps to a directory service.

A Principal has id, type, name, description, email, timeZone, capabilities and accounts. The type MUST be one of individual, group, resource, location or other. The standard get, changes, set, query and queryChanges methods apply; a server MUST reject any change it does not allow with a forbidden SetError. Where changes are supported, it SHOULD let users update their own name, description and timeZone.
sections.eli5: A principal is a name tag for a person, a team or even a room that things can be shared with.

sections.title: Capabilities and Subscribing
sections.content:
Two capability URIs are added. urn:ietf:params:jmap:principals signals support for Principal and ShareNotification; its account capability includes currentUserPrincipalId. urn:ietf:params:jmap:principals:owner appears only as a key in an Account's accountCapabilities, and holds accountIdForPrincipal and principalId for the Principal that owns the Account.

Permission says whether a user may access data, not whether they want to. A user can subscribe to what they care about. Servers MUST only include in the Session object Accounts where the user is subscribed to at least one record or which belong to the user, and StateChange events SHOULD only be sent for subscribed data.
sections.eli5: You may be allowed into every classroom, but you only put the ones you visit on your own timetable.

sections.title: ShareNotifications
sections.content:
A ShareNotification records when the user's permissions to a shared object change. Only the server creates them; clients may dismiss one by destroying it, and any attempt to create or update one MUST be rejected with forbidden. Its properties include created, changedBy, objectType, objectAccountId, objectId, oldRights, newRights and name.

The server SHOULD create one whenever the user's permissions change on an object. It MAY skip notifications for changes to a group Principal, MAY limit how many it stores (deleting the oldest first), and MAY coalesce or expire them.
sections.eli5: When someone gives you or takes away access, you get a little note saying who did it and what changed.

sections.title: The Framework for Shared Data
sections.content:
Shareable data types MUST define three properties. isSubscribed says whether the user wants to see the data. myRights is a map of permission names to booleans for the current user. shareWith is null if not shared, otherwise a map from Principal id to the rights given; the owner's Principal MUST NOT appear in it, since owner rights are implicit.

The RFC's worked example is a to-do list type with mayRead, mayWrite and mayAdmin rights. A client finds the Principal account through the principals:owner capability, fetches Principals with Principal/get and shares a list by updating shareWith.
sections.eli5: Every shareable thing keeps a guest list saying who may look, who may change it, and who may run it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
All JMAP security considerations apply. Four more are listed:

  • Spoofing: letting users edit their own Principal could let them imitate another user and trick others into sharing data. Servers may forbid it and SHOULD log such changes.
  • Unnoticed sharing: sharing can turn a brief account compromise into a persistent one; extra authorization or notifying the sharer by another channel can mitigate this.
  • Denial of service: many sharing changes can generate many ShareNotifications; coalescing and rate limiting help.
  • Unauthorized Principals: the set of Principals MUST be strictly controlled.
sections.eli5: Be careful who can pretend to be someone else, and who can quietly add themselves to the guest list.

sections.title: Registrations and Internationalization
sections.content:
IANA registered the capabilities urn:ietf:params:jmap:principals and urn:ietf:params:jmap:principals:owner and the data types Principal and ShareNotification.

On internationalization, servers MAY restrict the characters allowed in free-form string fields, for example using the FreeformClass of RFC 8264. A server can strip forbidden characters or reject the change with an invalidProperties SetError.
sections.eli5: The new names were officially written down in a public list, and servers can refuse odd characters in names.

viz.caption: THE THREE PROPERTIES SHAREABLE TYPES MUST DEFINE

items.title: isSubscribed
items.text: Whether the user wishes to see this data.

items.title: myRights
items.text: The permissions the current user has, as a map of names to booleans.

items.title: shareWith
items.text: Null, or a map from Principal id to the rights given to that Principal.
